shot.prose:
The page reads as a clean documentation layout — logo top-left, hamburger top-right, large "Core" heading, code block, prose, then cards. The overall column width fills the 390 px viewport sensibly without feeling cramped side-to-side.

The gap between the nav bar and the "Core" heading is strikingly large — perhaps 60–70 px of bare grey — which on an 844 px mobile viewport means the user has already spent roughly 15% of above-the-fold height before any content begins. The code block arrives soon after the heading and anchors attention quickly, which partially compensates, but the dead air before "Core" is the most obvious spatial waste on the screen.

Hierarchy is handled well: the bold lead phrases ("That is the whole mental model", "Three are not.") act as visual sub-heads without a formal `<h2>`, and the inline badges for component names (pink/salmon for `View`, `Page`, `App`; dark for `Router`, `Item`, `List`) carry an implicit semantic colour split that a returning reader will learn — this is a real strength.

That said, the second prose paragraph becomes genuinely dense: six or seven dark badges packed into five lines, an italic run spanning two lines, and an em-dash clause all compound together, making the eye work hard to find a rest point. Spacing between that paragraph and the one above it looks consistent with the gap below the code block, so the problem is internal density, not the paragraph margin.

The phrase "Item's own record" carries what appears to be an orange underline decoration — it reads more like a formatting artifact or a coloured underline than a clear hyperlink cue, especially surrounded by badges of similar warm hues; its affordance is ambiguous.

The two cards at the bottom ("View" and "Page") each have a white surface with a soft border and a small icon — they read as distinct surfaces and the icon glyphs, though tiny, add a touch of imagery that breaks the all-text block above. Alignment of the card left edge appears flush with the prose left margin, which is good.

Contrast is fine throughout: dark text on light grey body, light syntax-highlighted text on the dark code block, and the badge text colours appear legible against their respective fills.
